claims.text: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles contain five or more metals in near-equiatomic ratios and can form a single solid-solution phase.
The initial nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution and single-phase crystallinity.
The retained solid solution is metastable.
Retention of the single-phase solid solution over 473–1923 K is governed by kinetic limitations on atomic diffusion that oppose phase segregation.
Sufficiently small nanoparticles have limited atomic mobility even at the upper end of the stated operating-temperature range.
Inert or mildly reactive atmospheres help preserve phase homogeneity.
High configurational entropy favors a single solid-solution phase over intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Increasing the number of constituent elements dilutes each atom type and makes preferred ordering or segregation more difficult.
At high temperatures, thermodynamics would normally drive segregation in these nanoparticles.
Atomic-size-induced lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity in high-entropy alloys.
A solid, compositionally mixed precursor restricts atomic mobility during particle formation.
Restricted mobility in a solid precursor inhibits intermetallic ordering and elemental segregation.
The synthesis-time mobility restriction produced by a solid precursor persists during subsequent operation across 473–1923 K.
Larger particles can overcome kinetic limitations and consequently undergo phase segregation.
Strongly oxidizing or reducing atmospheres can promote diffusion sufficiently to cause phase changes.
Small nanoparticles under inert or mildly reactive conditions will remain single-phase, minimally segregated, and strained throughout 473–1923 K.
Larger particles or particles exposed to strongly oxidizing or reducing conditions will show segregation, intermetallic formation, or increased structural disorder.
Combined XRD and XAS can track single-phase alloy formation and changes in reduction or local chemical state.
Particle size and atmosphere will be varied while phase homogeneity, local coordination, oxidation state, and elemental segregation are measured.
The exact critical particle size and atmosphere depend on elemental combination and synthesis history and are not presently specified.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe larger particles as having longer diffusion paths, which would ordinarily strengthen a diffusion limitation, while the mechanism and prediction say that larger particles overcome the kinetic limitation and segregate. No additional size-dependent mobility or timescale argument resolves this internal tension.
